translations.answer: Not. When the contact force peak increases from 1e-6 to 1e6, it rises from 80 N to 110 N and the base speed fluctuations decrease. However, after reaching 1e14, large unstable contact force peaks and falling occur. A scan of contact force, velocity, and constraint residuals should be performed within a limited range, rather than increasing monotonically.
translations.applicability: This case is a single four-legged simulation observation, and the parameter scan must be re-done within the cost scaling of the target controller.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare contact force, base angular velocity, and linear velocity curves under different weights.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Reduce mpc_alpha to a level that can generate near-single-foot half-body contact force during the trot phase, and limitively increase floating_base_weight.
translations.details.environments.0: Four-legged robot trot simulation; robot mass example is ~20 kg, total gravity ~200 N.
translations.details.limits.0: Numerical results from a specific four-legged simulation, and the author explicitly states that the conclusion is still to be verified by others; cannot directly be copied to human-like robots or different normalized cost functions.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Contact force peak of the foot increases from 80 N to 110 N when floating_base_weight increases from 1e-6 to 1e6, and base speed fluctuations decrease. However, when floating_base_weight is increased to 1e14, instability and falling occur.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: The MPC contact force penalty weight is too large, leading to insufficient support force; the WBC floating base weight is too large, leading to unstable contact force.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: The weight scan must set limits on contact force, torque, and state; the 1e14 scale has already caused falling in simulation, and cannot be directly implemented on real machines.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: mpc_alpha is a force amplitude penalty term; too large suppresses contact force; too small may amplify the sensitivity of the real robot to acceleration changes.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The overlarge floating_base_weight excessively lowers the relaxation cost between dynamics and contact force.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Contact force is too small when mpc_alpha=0.1.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Contact force becomes sparse and large when floating_base_weight=1e14, leading to falling.
translations.media_summaries.0: Image 'mpc_alpha=0.1' simultaneously shows four-legged simulation and foot contact force curve; the curve amplitude is low, consistent with the text's description of insufficient support force, but the screenshot itself does not provide a uniform coordinate scale.
translations.media_summaries.1: Image 'floating_base_weight=1e6' shows a regular, periodic foot contact force waveform with peak around 110 N; this can be compared with the text's description of ~80 N at 1e-6.
translations.media_summaries.2: Image 'floating_base_weight=1e14' shows sparse and large contact force peaks, corresponding to the text's description of unstable contact force and falling.
translations.source.locator: Text 'wbc weight param' and fig3/fig6/1e14 unstable graph.
translations.source.title: Impact of MPC + WBC weight param on four-legged robots.
